full_judgment:
2. On 12.10.1997, one Md. Lokman Hossain Biswas, predecessor of the opposite-party nos. 1-8, as pre-emptor instituted Miscellaneous Case No. 59 of 1997 in the 1st Court of Joint District Judge, Kushtia against the pre-emptee-petitioner and others praying for pre-emption of the case property measuring an area of 01.37 decimals out of the total quantum of land of 16.44 decimals appertaining to S. A. plot no. 82 corresponding to R. S. plot no. 222 and S. A. Khatian No. 746 corresponding to R. S. Khatian No. 706 of Mouza Bahadurkhali, District- Kushtia under Section 24 of the Non-Agricultural Tenancy Act, 1949. During the pendency of the Miscellaneous Case, the original pre-emptor Md. Lokman Hossain Biswas died and his legal heirs, that is to say, opposite-party nos. 1-8 ware substituted in his place and as substituted pre-emptors, they prosecuted the pre-emption case against the pre-emptees and others in the Court of first instance. Anyway, the case of the pre-emptors, in short, is that the pre-emptors are co-sharers in the case plot. On 20.08.1997, the pre-emptee-seller Md. Abdul Jalil Biswas sold out the case property in favour of the pre-emptee-purchaser Md. Abdul Jabbar for consideration money of Tk. 1,85,000/- by a registered deed and at the time of sale; the pre-emptee-seller sold out some land in excess of his share. The pre-emptee-purchaser is a stranger to the case plot. However, the pre-emptors are entitled to the refund of Tk. 45,916/- for the sale of excess land to the extent of 00.34 decimals. After the purchase of the case property by the pre-emptee-purchaser, he instituted Partition Suit No. 16 of 1997 against the original pre-emptor Md. Lokman Hossain Biswas in the Civil Court and on receipt of the summons of the partition suit, Md. Lokman Hossain Biswas became aware of the purchase of the case property by the pre-emptee-purchaser from the pre-emptee-seller. As the substituted pre-emptors are co-sharers in the case plot, they are entitled to get the case properly by way of pre-emption under Section 24 of the Non Agricultural Tenancy Act. 

 4. After hearing the parties and on an assessment of the evidence and materials on record and in the facts and circumstances of the case, the trial Court dismissed the Pre-emption Case mainly on the score that the pre-emptors are not co-sharers in the case jote in view of the Mutation Khatian No. 706/1 standing in the name of the pre-emptee-seller Md. Abdul Jalil Biswas. 

 8. At the outset, Mr. Shasti Sarker, learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the pre-emptee-purchaser, submits that it is the admitted position that the pre-emptee-seller Md. Abdul Jalil Biswas was a co-sharer in the case plot and he got his share mutated in his name vide Mutation Case No. 12/IX-II/94-95 and consequently, a new Khatian being Mutation Khatian No. 706/1 was opened in the name of the pre-emptee-seller and since the jama was separated and a new Mutation Khatian was opened in the name of the pre-emptee-seller on 10.12.1994, the original pre-emptor, that is to say, Md. Lokman Hossain Biswas ceased to be a co-sharer in the case plot and that being so, the substituted pre-emptors are not entitled to get the case property by way of pre-emption. In support of his submission, Mr. Shasti Sarker relies upon the decisions in the cases of Shah Alam -Vs- Shahidur Rahman and others, 55 DLR (HCD) 214; Alfazuddin Ahmed-Vs- Abdur Rahman and others, 8 MLR (AD) 153 and Md. Khairullah Bhuiyan -Vs- Haji Nurul Alam Chowdhury, being dead his heirs: Amena Khatun and others, 35 DLR (AD) 338. 

 10. On the contrary, Mr. Md. Nurul Amin, learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the substituted pre-emptors (opposite-party nos. 1-8), submits that the lower Appellate Court did not contrail any error of law resulting in any error in its decision occasioning a failure of justice by holding that the substituted pre-emptors are co-sharers in the case plot and since they are co-sharers in the case plot, they are entitled to get the case property by way of pre-emption under Section 24 of the Non-Agricultural Tenancy Act albeit there might be a Mutation Khatian in the name of the pre-emptee-seller Md. Abdul Jalil Biswas. In order to buttress up this submission, Mr. Md. Nurul Amin draws my attention to the decision in the case of Md. Aminullah and others...Vs...Serajul Huq and others reported in 18 MLR (AD) 131. 

 13. A reference to the judgment of the Court of first instance indicates that it dismissed the Miscellaneous Case No. 59 of 1997 mainly on the ground that the jama is separated in view of the Mutation Khatian No. 706/1 standing in the name of the pre-emptee-seller Md. Abdul Jalil Biswas. 

 15. In the decision in the case of Alfazuddin Ahmed...Vs...Abdur Rahman and others reported in 8 MLR (AD) 153, it has been spelt out that separation of tenancy/jama khatian disentitles the petitioner to the right of pre-emption. 

 "12. In a case of pre-emption filed under Section 24 of the Non-Agricultural Tenancy Act, if a co-sharer tenant owns a portion of land in any plot, he is to be treated as co-sharer in the entire plot even if the land of that plot is recorded in more than one khatian. Therefore, in the event of transfer of a portion of land of that plot appertaining to another khatian, a co-sharer tenant can file a pre-emption case under Section 24 of the Non-Agricultural Tenancy Act, notwithstanding the fact that he does not have any interest in that khatian. The words 'one or more co-sharer tenants of such land' occurring in Section 24 of the Non-Agricultural Tenancy Act means a co-sharer in the plot and not in the holding as mentioned in Section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. Such' being the position of law, the pre-emptors are not even required to file an application for amendment to show that they have also interest in R. S. Khatian No. 3838. 

 18. From the above principle of law, it is crystal clear that a person seeking pre-emption of any non-agricultural land under Section 24 of the Non-Agricultural Tenancy Act must be a co-sharer in the plot even if the land of that plot is recorded in more than one khatian. The R. S. Khatian of the case plot is 706 and the Mutation Khatian No. 706/1 stands in the name of the pre-emptee-seller Md. Abdul Jalil Biswas vide Mutation Case No. 12/IX-11/94-95. It is the admitted position that the R. S. case plot no. is 222 corresponding to S. A. plot no. 82 and the quantum of land of the entire case plot is 16.44 decimals and the land sought to be pre-empted is 01.37 decimals. So it is seen that with regard to the case plot, there are two Khatians, namely, R. S. Khatian No. 706 and Mutation Khatian No. 706/1 and both these Khatians relate to the R. S. plot no. 222 corresponding to S. A. plot no. 82. Following the 'ratio decidendi' of the decision reported in 18 MLR (AD) 131, I am left with no option but to hold that the substituted pre-emptors are necessarily co-sharers in the case plot, though it appertains to two Khatians, namely, R. S. Khatian No. 706 and Mutation Khatian No. 706/1. From that decision, it is also abundantly clear that the expression 'non-agricultural land' used in Section 24 of the Non-Agricultural Tenancy Act is not synonymous with the word 'holding' as used is the Bengal Tenancy Act or the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act.
